props.title: Beyond the Sea
props.initialSlug: Kevin Spacey embodies Bobby Darin's rise to stardom

sections.content: Beyond the Sea (2004) represents Kevin Spacey's passionate tribute to Bobby Darin, delivering both as director and star in this unconventional biopic. The film follows the template established by All That Jazz (1979), using fantasy sequences and breaking the fourth wall to tell Darin's story. Like Rocketman (2019), it eschews strict biographical accuracy in favor of capturing the spirit and energy of its subject through elaborate musical numbers and dreamlike sequences. Spacey's dedication shows in his actual singing of Darin's hits, similar to how Joaquin Phoenix embodied Johnny Cash in Walk the Line (2005).

sections.content: The mid-2000s marked a golden era for musical biopics, with Ray (2004) and Walk the Line (2005) setting new standards for the genre. While these films took more traditional approaches, Beyond the Sea dared to experiment with form, much like I'm Not There (2007) would later do with Bob Dylan's story. The film's meta-narrative structure, where Darin reflects on his own life while making a movie about it, predates similar techniques used in Rocketman (2019) and Elvis (2022).

Spacey's film particularly excels in its recreation of 1950s and 1960s showbiz atmosphere, reminiscent of the period detail in La La Land (2016). The musical numbers capture the energy of classic Hollywood musicals like Singin' in the Rain (1952), while maintaining a contemporary edge in their staging and choreography. The film's exploration of Darin's drive for fame parallels similar themes in Jersey Boys (2014) and Bohemian Rhapsody (2018). SUBHEAD: Breaking Biopic Conventions

sections.content: What sets Beyond the Sea apart is its willingness to break conventional biopic rules. Like Velvet Goldmine (1998), it creates a heightened reality that better serves the emotional truth of its subject than strict historical accuracy. The film's innovative structure influenced later works like Love & Mercy (2014), which used multiple actors and timelines to portray Brian Wilson of the Beach Boys.
